name: Curated Quake II map studies, first cycle
scope: Local reference analysis and structured playtest preparation; multiplayer-first. Selection is a study hypothesis, not a new quality rating.

lessons.title: 01 — Recognizable spaces and route choice
lessons.question: From each spawn, identify the first landmark, first useful weapon, two route choices and a return route. Which cues let a new player predict where a route goes?

lessons.title: 02 — Vertical combat and asymmetric return paths
lessons.question: Compare upper/lower control, upward access, safe retreat, drops and teleporter exits. Does gaining height create a decision, and what can the lower player do in response?

lessons.title: 03 — Item economies and contestable control
lessons.question: Trace armor, major health and strong-weapon circuits. Measure actual travel time and exposure before assigning an advantage to proximity or height.

lessons.title: 04 — Alternating combat ranges and room proportions
lessons.question: Mark close, medium and long engagements, ceiling clearance, cover, narrow thresholds and open courts. Does each transition offer a distinct tactical choice?

lessons.title: 05 — Theme, landmarks, materials and light
lessons.question: Inspect landmark silhouettes, material families, light hierarchy and sound cues in engine. Separate archive theme labels from what the rendered map actually communicates.

lessons.title: 06 — FFA scale, encounters and congestion
lessons.question: Run the documented low and high player loads. Track encounter intervals, empty travel, spawn pressure and congestion; distinguish intentional breathing space from wasted space.

lessons.title: 07 — CTF routes, bases and return pressure
lessons.question: Verify the required CTF game module, then test both teams, both base exits and flag-return routes. Compare access to weapons/resources before considering visual symmetry.

lessons.title: 08 — Detail that supports navigation
lessons.question: Inspect stairs, ramps, ledges, trims, collision silhouettes and sightline interruptions. Source files are present, but authored origin and permissions still require verification before source training.

lessons.title: 09 — Remakes and the difference between variety and reskinning
lessons.question: Compare authorship, recorded lineage and gameplay descriptors. Identify which choices change control and flow, and which only change presentation. Keep all related works in one partition.

lessons.title: 10 — Validation authors, used to tune the rubric
lessons.question: Apply the frozen rubric and reference bands to these authors. Record justified exceptions and adjust the rubric here, with a version change, before opening final test results.

lessons.title: 11 — Reserved authors for a prospective final evaluation
lessons.question: Freeze generator, prompts, seeds and rubric first. Have reviewers compare blinded generated/reference pairs; report all failures and preferences. Never tune on this partition after inspecting results.

lessons.title: 12 — Large-map boundary case
lessons.question: Audit this archive-labelled 24–64-player map as a scale boundary. Resolve its author and metadata before admitting it to any reference profile; do not extrapolate duel defaults to it.
